subject: Tenant data tenure & deletion (Hosted API) — RFI
messages:
From: Amelia Rose <amelia.rose@helixhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Security <security@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: tenant data tenure / deletion practices (hosted API)

Hi Irene,

Thanks for making time yesterday. As part of our security review we still need a concise, auditable explanation of how Redwood handles tenant-scoped data retention and deletion for the Hosted API. Specifically we need answers to the following items so we can close the ticket: 

1) How long is tenant request/response data retained by default (control-plane logs, embedded payloads, and model input/event traces)?
2) If a customer requests deletion of a tenant, what is the exact sequence and timeline for purging data from:
   - live request store (short-term caches),
   - object backups and cold storage,
   - logs and telemetry (traces, metrics exports), and
   - backups / snapshots that might contain encrypted blobs?
3) Do you provide a way to scope deletions to only specific datasets (e.g., prompt history vs. billing metadata)?
4) How are legal holds / e-discovery handled (can retention be overridden; what is the process)?

We prefer short bullet answers and any pointer to artifacts (playbooks / matrices) you can share.

Appreciate it — aim is to have this included in our vendor assessment by 11/20.

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Rose
Senior Information Security Manager, Helix Health
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Rose <amelia.rose@helixhealth.com>
Cc: DevOps Security <security@helixhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: tenant data tenure / deletion practices (hosted API)

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers plus two attachments: a retention matrix (spreadsheet) and our erasures playbook (PDF). Attachment stubs: redwood_hosted_tenant_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (XLSX), erasures_playbook.pdf (PDF).

1) Default retention windows (short bullets):
   - Request/response payloads (model inputs & outputs): retained for 30 days by default for debugging and rate-limiting analysis.
   - Control-plane logs (auth events, routing decisions): retained 90 days by default; sensitive logs are redacted earlier per our logging policy.
   - Audit trails (policy/consent events): retained 365 days by default unless customer contract specifies otherwise.
   - Embeddings/derived artifacts: not stored by default for Hosted API unless the customer opts in; if stored, retention matches their configured TTL.

2) Deletion sequence & timelines (upon customer-initiated full-tenant erasure request):
   - T+0: We acknowledge request and create a deletion ticket.
   - T+ <24 hours: Disable new writes for the tenant (prevent further data ingestion).
   - T+1–3 days: Purge live request stores and KV caches (prefix/KV cache eviction).
   - T+3–7 days: Remove objects from hot/cold object stores and mark related DB rows for deletion (logical delete + async hard delete).
   - T+7–30 days: Expunge from backups and snapshots on the next backup rotation (we do not keep separate long-term immutable copies beyond contractual backups). For encrypted backup blobs, keys are scheduled for revocation in coordination with KMS policies to accelerate practical unrecoverability.
   - T+30–90 days: Sanitization of analytics pipelines and derivative artifacts (retrain queues, feature stores) where applicable; where full immediate purge is impractical we provide attestations and a rollout schedule.

   Notes: timelines above are our default SLOs for Hosted API customers; enterprise contracts can shorten or lengthen windows. We provide a deletion confirmation report when the process completes.

3) Scoped deletions: yes. We support scoped erasures by category: 'conversation history' (prompt/response), 'billing metadata', and 'custom attachments'. Scoped requests are handled via our ticketing API; expected completion depends on scope (usually 48–72 hours for in-scope live stores).

4) Legal holds / EDD: legal holds are supported. When a valid legal hold is presented by the customer (signed POA or compliance request), we suspend automatic deletions for the affected tenant and maintain an auditable hold record. Holds require sign-off from our compliance team; we will surface estimated timelines for resuming deletion once the hold is lifted.

References/Artifacts: retention matrix and erasures playbook attached. Also: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c (high-level runbook) and HubSpot record HS-12345.

If you want I can run a short live walkthrough with our Ops owner (Jonas) — we can demo the deletion ticket flow and the attestation artifact.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
From: DevOps Security <security@helixhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: tenant data tenure / deletion practices (hosted API)

Hi Irene / Jonas — quick follow-up from our compliance review: 

- Can you confirm whether backups are rotated on a strict schedule or if you retain immutable snapshots beyond 90 days? Helix policy requires that vendor backups containing PHI be erased within 90 days of a deletion request unless there is a contractual retention requirement.
- For encrypted backup blobs, can you explain the KMS key revocation process (is revocation immediate or scheduled) and whether key revocation alone is considered sufficient evidence of unrecoverability?

Appreciate a short answer we can include in our vendor binder.

— Amela (on behalf of Helix DevOps Security)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: DevOps Security <security@helixhealth.com>, Amelia Rose <amelia.rose@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: tenant data tenure / deletion practices (hosted API)

Hi Amelia — quick clarifications from Ops: 

- Backups: We run scheduled backups with a 30/90/365 tiering cadence depending on service component. For Hosted API tenant data, any snapshot that contains tenant-scoped payloads is marked and scheduled for expedited expunge on the next rotation; our standard practice is to fully remove tenant-containing snapshots within 90 days of a validated deletion request unless a contract requires longer. We will document this as a policy clause for Helix specifically.

- KMS / key revocation: We use customer-agnostic KMS keys for backups in Hosted environments. When a tenant deletion reaches the backup-expunge step, we schedule key rotation/revocation for the snapshot encryption keys linked to that tenant. Key revocation is executed via our KMS provider API and is typically scheduled within the same 7–30 day window noted earlier. Key revocation + snapshot expunge together form our practical unrecoverability approach; we provide a signed attestation after both steps complete.

If you'd like a short paragraph we can drop into your vendor binder, here's a suggested one you can paste: 

"Redwood Inference (Hosted API): tenant-scoped request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default. Upon a validated tenant erasure request Redwood will (1) disable writes immediately, (2) purge live caches and object stores within 7 days, (3) remove tenant-containing snapshots within 90 days (expedited where contractually required), and (4) coordinate KMS key revocation to render backups unrecoverable. A final deletion attestation is issued when the workflow completes."

Let me know if you want the exact wording adjusted.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference
